tune help

tune reads your Claude Code session transcripts, shows where the tokens went and offers fixes. Everything runs locally with node. Nothing gets sent anywhere.

This page covers what tune reads, how to read the report, every tip and fix, how tracking works and where tune keeps its files. Open it any time with:

node dist/tune.cjs help --open

Quick start

  1. Run /tune:tune in a Claude Code session (or /tune if nothing else uses that name).
  2. Claude runs the scan and walks you through the tips, your costliest sessions and your hot files.
  3. Pick the fixes you want. Claude asks before applying any of them.
  4. Run /tune again in a week or two to see whether the tips you took helped.

The first scan reads every transcript and can take a few seconds. Later scans only read what changed.

What tune reads

Claude Code saves every session as a JSONL file under ~/.claude/projects, one folder per working directory. Subagent transcripts sit in a folder next to the session. tune reads all of them.

It does not matter where the session ran. The CLI, the VS Code extension, the desktop app, claude -p and the Agent SDK all save to the same folder, and the report tells you which one each session came from:

Label Where it ran
CLI claude in a terminal
VS Code The Claude Code extension for VS Code
Desktop The Claude desktop app
claude -p claude -p, the non-interactive mode scripts use
Agent SDK A program built on the Agent SDK
unknown The transcript does not say

A few things are left out:

  • Sessions with no requests. You opened them and left, so they say nothing about how you work.
  • Deleted transcripts. Claude Code deletes a transcript 30 days after its last use unless cleanupPeriodDays says otherwise. tune keeps what it measured for a year, but it cannot measure a session it never saw. The transcript-cleanup tip covers this.

If you set CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, tune reads that folder instead of ~/.claude, the same way Claude Code does.

What the dollar figures mean

Every cost is worked out at API list price from the token counts in the transcripts. That is what the same work would cost on the API. On a Pro or Max plan you do not pay that amount, but the figures still show which sessions and habits use up your limits fastest.

The report

tune report prints the report as Markdown. /tune reads it and walks you through it. It has these parts, in order.

Totals. The number of sessions, what they cost, how much of it went to re-reading cached context, what went to subagents, and the average and largest context. The next line splits sessions and spend by where they ran.

Where the spend went. The cost split by what filled the context:

Slice What it is
System prompt and tool definitions Claude Code's own prompt and the tool definitions sent with every request
CLAUDE.md and memory Your instruction files, sent with every request
Skills The skill list and the body of each skill a session loaded
Hooks and reminders Hook output and notes Claude Code adds to the conversation as it goes
Reading files Files Claude read, carried for the rest of the session
Command and search output Shell output, search results and other tool results
Web and connectors Web search, web fetch and MCP connector results
Code and commands Claude wrote What Claude put in tool calls, like file edits and commands
Subagent reports What subagents sent back to the main session
Prompts, replies and thinking Your prompts and Claude's replies, carried from turn to turn
Writing replies (output tokens) The tokens Claude wrote in each response

Every request sends the whole conversation again, so something read early in a long session is paid for on every request after it. That is why reading files and command output are often the biggest slices.

Tips. What stands out across your sessions, worst first. Each one has a finding with numbers, advice, what following the advice gives up, when to skip it, the sessions that show it worst and the fixes on offer. See Tips.

Costliest sessions. Up to 8 sessions that cost $3 or more, each with where and when it ran, its context size, the spend split, the causes that drove the cost and what fixing each would save, and the heaviest items it carried.

Hot files. Files that sessions kept reading, by what carrying them in context cost. A file shows up once at least 2 sessions read it. Short, focused files are cheaper to read, so a big hot file is a good one to split.

Suggested skills and agents. Skills and agents tune can write for you, with the reason it suggests each one. See Fixes.

Tips

Each tip has an id you use with fix and track, and a severity: high, medium or low. A tip only shows when it is worth acting on.

file-reads (high)

Files read once are paid for on every later request. A file read on request 20 of a 400 request session is sent 380 more times. Hand searches to a subagent such as scout, read line ranges instead of whole files, and keep the files sessions read most short.

Fixes: split the hot files (launch), add the scout agent (create). Skip it for short sessions, which pay little to carry a file.

context-reread (high)

Most of the spend is re-reading old context. The 300th turn of a session costs far more than the 3rd. Start a new session when you move on to a new task, use /clear when you switch to something unrelated, and /compact with a focus at natural breakpoints.

Fixes: compact at 200K tokens (knob), add the scout agent (create). Skip it in the middle of hard debugging. Write a handoff note first and start fresh once that task is done.

huge-context (high)

Sessions grow huge without compacting. Lower autoCompactWindow so Claude Code compacts long before the 1M limit, or write a handoff note and carry on in a fresh session.

Fixes: compact at 200K tokens (knob), add the handoff skill (create). Skip it for work that needs a lot in view at once, like a refactor across many files.

unused-tools (medium)

Every request carries tools that never get used. A tool's definition goes out with every request whether Claude calls it or not. Adding a tool to permissions.deny leaves it out of the request.

Fix: deny the tools you never use (knob). Keep a tool you use now and then, even if only in a few sessions.

heavy-skills (medium)

Skills cost more to carry than they need to. A loaded skill stays in context for the rest of the session. Keep SKILL.md to the steps Claude needs every time and move reference material into files it reads only when needed.

Fix: slim the heaviest skills (launch). Skip it for short skills or ones used only in short sessions.

idle-rewrite (medium)

Resuming big sessions after a break rewrites the cache. The prompt cache expires after a few minutes without a request. Coming back to a 500K session after lunch writes all of it again, about $2.50 at Opus prices.

Fixes: compact at 200K tokens (knob), add the handoff skill (create). Skip it for short breaks.

subagent-model (medium)

Subagents run on the most expensive models. Most subagent work is searching and summarizing, which Sonnet or Haiku do well for a fraction of the price.

Fixes: run subagents on Sonnet with CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL (knob), add the scout agent on Haiku (create). Keep Opus for agents that review code, plan or debug by giving them model: opus in their frontmatter.

big-results (medium)

Huge tool output stays in context. Filter output before Claude sees it, ask for line ranges, or cap Bash output with BASH_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH.

Fixes: cap shell output at 15,000 characters (knob), add the quiet-run skill (create). Let the full output through when you do not know yet what you are looking for.

repeated-commands (medium)

The same commands run over and over. Polling a build, server or CI run from the main session sends the whole context again each time.

Fixes: add the ci-watch agent, the dev-server skill and the quiet-run skill (create). A quick test or build you rerun after each small edit is fine.

long-sessions (medium)

Long sessions mix several tasks. Keep one task per session and put facts every session needs in CLAUDE.md or a skill.

Fixes: compact at 200K tokens (knob), add the handoff skill (create). Stay in one session when the tasks build on each other.

denials (medium)

Tool calls keep getting denied. Each denied call is a wasted turn. Add allow rules for the read-only commands Claude keeps asking for.

Fix: run /fewer-permission-prompts in the project with the most denials (launch). Keep denying anything that pushes, deletes, deploys or touches production.

instructions (low)

CLAUDE.md and memory are sent with every request. Keep them to one line per rule.

Fix: have Claude tighten ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md and the memory index (launch). Leave a rule long when its detail prevents a costly mistake.

rereads (low)

Files are read again and again. Each read of a whole file adds it to context again. Ask for the lines you need, or grep for them.

Fix: add the scout agent (create). A reread after the file changed is worth it.

tool-errors (low)

Many tool calls fail. Put the exact build, test and lint commands, and the setup they need, in CLAUDE.md.

Fix: have Claude find the failing commands and add the right ones to the project's CLAUDE.md (launch). Failing tests and type errors do not count. They are how Claude finds problems.

cd-commands (low)

Commands keep changing folders. Start sessions in the project folder, so its CLAUDE.md and skills load, and use absolute paths or git -C instead of cd. Claude Code puts the shell back in the session folder after a cd outside it, so every later command there starts with cd again.

Fix: add the folders sessions keep going to to permissions.additionalDirectories (knob), so the shell stays after one cd. Sessions can then also read and edit files there. Work across several repos cannot always avoid it.

transcript-cleanup (low)

Claude Code deletes old transcripts. It shows once your oldest session is close to the cleanupPeriodDays limit (30 days by default) and the setting is under 90 days. Raising it lets tune measure sessions it never scanned in time, and lets /resume reach them.

Fix: keep transcripts for 90 days (knob). Transcripts take disk space roughly in proportion to the days kept, so skip it when disk space is tight.

Fixes

Every fix has an id like knob:autoCompactWindow. The report lists them under each tip. There are three kinds.

knob sets one key in ~/.claude/settings.json. Environment settings like CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL go in its env block. If the file is a symlink into a dotfiles repo, tune writes through the link, so the link stays. A copy of the old file goes in the backups folder first. A knob already set the way the fix wants shows as already applied. New sessions pick up the change.

create writes a skill or agent into ~/.claude/skills or ~/.claude/agents. It never overwrites a file that is already there, and one already in the project's .claude folder counts as done.

Id Kind What it does
handoff skill Writes a short handoff note so you can /clear or start fresh without losing the thread
scout agent A read-only search agent on Haiku that returns only the answer
quiet-run skill Runs builds and tests with output in a log file and brings back only the errors
land skill Commits, rebases onto the default branch, reruns checks, pushes and removes the worktree
ci-watch agent Waits on a GitHub Actions run on Haiku and reports only the result or the failing lines
dev-server skill Starts, restarts and stops local servers in the background and waits until they answer

launch is a task Claude does in the session, like splitting a big file or trimming a skill. tune fix <id> prints the task, the folder to do it in and whether to make a new worktree. Claude shows it to you and asks before starting.

Use --dry-run to see what a knob or create fix would do without doing it.

Tracking

Applying a knob or create fix starts tracking the tips it follows. You can also track a tip by hand with tune track <tip-id>, which is how you mark a habit change, like starting fresh sessions more often.

Once a tip is tracked, a later report compares the sessions that started after that moment with the sessions from the 30 days before. Sessions that were already running when tracking started are left out. It compares:

  • the habit the tip is about, like average context or denials,
  • the cost per prompt,
  • the side effects the tip warns about.

The verdict is one of:

Verdict Meaning
better The habit improved and nothing it could cost got worse
mixed The habit improved, but a side effect got worse
same Nothing moved more than 10%
worse The habit, or a side effect, got worse
early Fewer than 5 sessions have run since tracking started
no-baseline There were no sessions in the 30 days before to compare with

A tracked tip stays in the report even once the habit no longer stands out, so you can still see how it went. Stop tracking it with tune track <tip-id> --off.

Command line

The skill runs dist/tune.cjs with node, and you can run it yourself from the plugin folder:

node dist/tune.cjs report                 # Markdown report
node dist/tune.cjs report --json          # everything, as JSON
node dist/tune.cjs fix <fix-id> --dry-run # what a fix would do
node dist/tune.cjs fix <fix-id>           # apply a fix
node dist/tune.cjs track <tip-id> [--off] # start or stop tracking a tip
node dist/tune.cjs help                   # the commands
node dist/tune.cjs help --open            # this page, in your browser

With no command, it runs report. You can also pass any of these to the skill, like /tune fix knob:autoCompactWindow.

The installed plugin lives under ~/.claude/plugins. In a Claude Code session, ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} points at it.

Files and settings

tune keeps its own files outside the plugin folder, since a plugin update replaces that folder:

File What it holds
tuning.json What tune measured for each session, so a rescan only reads transcripts that changed
tuning-tracked.json The tips you track and since when
backups/ Copies of settings.json from before each change tune made

They live in ${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/claude-tune. These environment variables change where things go:

Variable Effect
CLAUDE_TUNE_STATE_DIR Where tune keeps its own files
XDG_STATE_HOME The base for the default state folder
CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR Where Claude Code keeps transcripts and settings, ~/.claude by default

tune reads settings the way Claude Code layers them, so it can tell whether a fix is already in place. From highest to lowest: managed settings, the project's .claude/settings.local.json and .claude/settings.json, ~/.claude/settings.json, then the environment. It only ever writes the user file.

After an update that changes what tune measures, the next scan reads every transcript again. That takes a few seconds once.

Troubleshooting

It says there are no sessions. Check that ~/.claude/projects (or $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects) has .jsonl files in it. Sessions with no requests do not count.

My VS Code sessions are missing. They save to the same folder as the CLI, so they show up under the VS Code label. If you set CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR in the extension's claudeCode.environmentVariables setting, run tune with the same value.

A fix says it is not on offer. Fixes only show while their tip applies. Run report to see the current list. Skills and agents can always be created with fix create:<id>.

help --open did not open anything. It uses open on macOS and xdg-open on Linux. Without a desktop, like over ssh, open the path it prints yourself.

node complains. tune needs node 22.3 or later on your PATH.
